supersedes: Spec 0.3 proposal to parameterize the stage-3-batch.js lifecycle by boundary.

decisions.question: Stage 4 migration tooling
decisions.statement: Do NOT parameterize the 17-step stage-3-batch.js lifecycle (it carries per-batch releases, before-images and history replays, removed by D3/D4). Four steps: (1) plan, dry run: targets, consumers, tier A/B/C, expected edge and bridge delta; (2) apply: ESM targets, activation shims, runtime contract, bridge registry, Manifest, runtime build, reusing the Stage 3 building blocks (shim renderer, runtime builder, bridge identity, Manifest observation), not their lifecycle wrapper; (3) verify: guards plus tier evidence (C: guards + game-cycle; B: public-API parity; A: hot-loop traces and save round-trip); (4) release only at a milestone: version bump, 1-3 CHANGELOG lines, owner play check.

decisions.question: Cluster record
decisions.statement: One small JSON per cluster (tier, hashes before/after, parity digest, guard results, edge/bridge delta): kilobytes, no before-images. Rollback is git revert.

decisions.question: Budgets
decisions.statement: All new Stage 4 tooling stays under ~2,000 lines; a new module needs at least two planned uses; once the cluster path works, archive tooling only Stage 3 needed (domain audit, per-batch artifacts) so utils/ shrinks. No new check file per cluster: one data-driven check validates all cluster records. Quick and Architecture stay under ~1 minute each. Behavior tests are grouped by game area (inventory, fight, input), not by migration step. Milestone report: lines in src/, utils/, architecture/ plus counts of classic scripts in index.html, baseline globals and bridges; if utils/ or architecture/ grow faster than scripts and bridges shrink, stop and simplify.

decisions.question: Later (Stage 5)
decisions.statement: Once the game boots from game.entry.js, replace the custom guards with a standard tool (dependency-cruiser or eslint-plugin-boundaries).
